BURSEVI:v6p220/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p220/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p220/r5.claim: Shuayb asks whether they fear the punishment of their Lord for associating partners with Him.

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2811/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2811/r1.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2811/r1.claim: Shuayb was also sent to the people of the thicket, herders who moved to a spring-fed grove when lowlands dried; he warned them, but they denied him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2811/r1.anchor: عن الربيع قال : ان شعيبا اخا مدين ارسل ايضا إلى اصحاب الايكة وهم كانوا قوم من اهل عمور يتبعون الرعاء والكلا في زمانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p184/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p184/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p184/r1.claim: Shuaib opens with the same kind of summons used by earlier messengers, for the reason Ibn Ashur has explained before.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p184/r1.anchor: وافتتح شعيب دعوته بمثل دعوات الرسل من قبله للوجه الذي قدمناه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p184/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p184/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p184/r2.claim: The call ألا تتقون includes forbidding shirk, since Shuaib's people were polytheists, as another passage in Hud states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p184/r2.anchor: فقد كانوا مشركين كما في آية سورة هود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r6.claim: The people reportedly had seven towns, and Shuʿayb was not one of them; he was from Midian, which is why he is called their brother elsewhere.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r7.claim: The prophets' repeated invocation uses the same wording because the faith they call people to is one and the same.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r7.anchor: وجاءت الألفاظ في دعاء كل واحد من هؤلاء الأنبياء واحدة بعينها إذ كان الإيمان المدعو إليه معنى واحدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r8.claim: The question ألا تتقون is a gentle, tactful appeal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p241#2/r8.anchor: وفي قولهم عليهم السلام ألا تتقون عرض رقيق وتلطف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p141#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p141#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p141#2/r1.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman says Shuʿayb is not called the “brother” of the people of the Thicket because he was not descended from them; he was sent to them after Midian, whose lineage he shared.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p141#2/r1.anchor: أن شعيبا لم يكن من نسل أصحاب الأيكة فلذلك لم يقل أخوهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p141#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p141#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p141#2/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says Midian was punished by the canopy; if Midian differed from the Thicket people, the two groups shared a fate, while Ibn Jarir identifies them as the same people and explains the omitted “brother” as brevity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p141#2/r2.anchor: أهل مدين عذبوا بعذاب الظلة فإن كانوا غير أصحاب الأيكة كما زعم مقاتل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.claim: The people of the Thicket are the people of Midian; Shuaib was their kinsman, but the Quran omits their brother from the address because they were associated with worship of the Thicket tree.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.claim: Some readers mistakenly treat Midian and the people of the Thicket as separate nations, so they claim Shuaib was sent to two or even three peoples.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.anchor: فزعم أن شعيبا عليه السلام، بعثه الله إلى أمتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r3.claim: A weak report says Shuaib alone among prophets was sent twice, first to Midian, destroyed by a blast, then to the Thicket people, destroyed by the cloud-day punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r3.anchor: إسحاق بن بشر الكاهلي -وهو ضعيف -حدثني ابن السدي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r4.claim: Qatādah identifies Shuaib's people with both the people of the Well and the people of the Thicket.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r5.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet calls Midian and the Thicket people two nations sent Shuaib, but Ibn Kathīr calls it strange, questions its raised attribution, and prefers that they were one community described differently.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r5.anchor: وهذا غريب، وفي رفعه نظر، والأشبه أن يكون موقوفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r6.claim: The same warning to these people to give full measure and weight as in the Midian account confirms that the two names describe one people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p158#2/r6.anchor: والصحيح أنهم أمة واحدة، وصفوا في كل مقام بشيء

MUQATIL:26:176-180/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:176-180/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:176-180/r2.claim: Shuaib asks whether they fear God, declares himself a trustworthy messenger, urges obedience, and says he asks no payment for belief: his reward rests only with the Lord of the worlds.
MUQATIL:26:176-180/r2.anchor: ولم يكن شعيب من نسبهم، فلذلك لم يقل عز وجل أخوهم شعيب،

QURTUBI-FULL:26:176-179/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:176-179/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:176-179/r13.claim: The opening admonition asks whether the people fear God; the next words identify Shuʿayb as a trustworthy messenger commanding them to obey.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:176-179/r13.anchor: { ألا تتقون } تخافون الله { إني لكم رسول أمين

TAB-FULL:v17p632#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p632#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p632#2/r1.claim: Al-aykah is a dense thicket and the singular of ayk; Arabs call any densely intertwined trees an aykah. The poet al-Nābighah uses it of a dove's grove.
TAB-FULL:v17p632#2/r1.anchor: تجلو بقادمتي حمامة أيكة … بردا أسف لثاته بالإثمد

TAB-FULL:v17p634/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p634/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p634/r1.claim: Shuayb asks his people to fear punishment for disobeying their Lord; he is God's trustworthy messenger carrying revelation, and obedience to him leads to right guidance.
TAB-FULL:v17p634/r1.anchor: ألا تتقون عقاب الله على معصيتكم ربكم

TABATABAI:26:176-177/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:176-177/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:176-177/r2.claim: Shuʿayb was an outsider to the Aykah people, explaining why the text says he addressed them without calling him their brother, unlike Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, and Lot, who had kinship ties.
TABATABAI:26:176-177/r2.anchor: وكان أجنبيا منهم ولذلك قيل { إذ قال لهم شعيب } ولم يقل أخوهم شعيب بخلاف هود وصالح

TABRISI:26:176-184/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:176-184/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:176-184/r9.claim: The text does not call Shuʿayb their brother because he was from Midian, not their kin; elsewhere it calls him the brother of Midian.
TABRISI:26:176-184/r9.anchor: ولم يقل أخوهم لأنه لم يكن من نسبهم وكان من أهل مدين

TABRISI:26:176-184/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:176-184/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:176-184/r10.claim: The repeated formula for the prophets signals their one message: fear God, avoid sins, worship sincerely, and obey messengers; prophets are trustworthy and take no fee, avoiding a deterrent to acceptance.
TABRISI:26:176-184/r10.anchor: حكى الله سبحانه دعوة كل نبي بصيغة واحدة ولفظ واحد إشعارا بأن الحق الذي تأتي به الرسل

THALABI:v7p178/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p178/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p178/r1.claim: The Thamud? The passage identifies the people of the thicket as Shu'ayb’s people; al-Ayka and al-Layka are two dialectal forms, both read in the Qur'an.
THALABI:v7p178/r1.anchor: كذب أصحاب الأيكة الغيضة وهم قوم شعيب والليكة والأيكة لغتان

THALABI:v7p178/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p178/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
THALABI:v7p178/r2.claim: Abu Zayd says God sent Shu'ayb to his own people of Midian and also to the nomadic people of the thicket.
THALABI:v7p178/r2.anchor: قال أبو زيد : بعث الله سبحانه شعيبا إلى قومه وأهل مدين وإلى أهل البادية

THALABI:v7p178/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p178/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p178/r3.claim: The verse does not call Shu'ayb their brother because he was not genealogically one of the thicket people; it does call him Midian’s brother because he belonged to them.
THALABI:v7p178/r3.anchor: ولم يقل أخوهم شعيب لأنه لم يكن من أصحاب الأيكة في النسب

THALABI:v7p178/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p178/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p178/r4.claim: The prophets’ repeated call to fear and obey God, worship sincerely, and seek no payment shows that their truth is one and their message is shared.
THALABI:v7p178/r4.anchor: وإنما دعوة هؤلاء الأنبياء كلهم فيما حكى الله سبحانه عنهم على صيغة واحدة

ASAD-NOTES:26:176#n74/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:176#n74/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:176#n74/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to his note on 7:85 and says Shu‘ayb’s story with Midian is told in greater detail at 11:84-95.
ASAD-NOTES:26:176#n74/r1.anchor: is given in greater detail in 11:84-95

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r1.claim: Shuʿayb descended from Midian, Abraham’s descendant, and was not one of the People of the Thicket; he was sent to both groups, so he is called their brother with Midian but not with the Thicket people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: شعيب كان من مدين؛ لأنه شعيب بن بويب بن مدين ابن إبراهيم خليل الرحمن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Shuʿayb was sent to his own people and to another people; the People of the Thicket were from Juthām.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r2.anchor: ابن عباس في هذه الآية: إن شعيبا بعث إلى قومه، وإلى غير قومه، وهو من ولد مدين بن إبراهيم، وأصحاب الأيكة من جذام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r3.claim: The repeated formula in this sūra shows that all prophets made one shared call: piety, obedience, exclusive worship, and asking no payment for preaching.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r3.anchor: دعوتهم كانت (¬3) على وجه # واحد] (¬1) وأنهم كانوا متفقين على الأمر بالتقوى والطاعة والإخلاص في العبادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r4.claim: The common prophetic message also included refraining from taking payment for the call and delivery of the message.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p117#2/r4.anchor: والامتناع من أخذ الأجر على الدعوى وتبليغ الرسالة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p521/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p521/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p521/r2.claim: “Will you not fear God?” means “Will you not be wary of God?” and repeats the earlier exhortation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p443/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p443/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p443/r1.claim: The section recounts Shu‘ayb and the people of Madyan: as Lot warned about moral misconduct, Shu‘ayb warned about economic misconduct; they persisted and met the other nations' fate, and the account closes with repeated verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p443/r1.anchor: Just as Lot (sws) warned his nation of their moral misconduct, Shu‘ayb (sws) warned his nation of economic misconduct.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p444/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p444/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p444/r4.claim: The opening verses repeat material from the preceding prophetic account and have already been explained.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p444/r4.anchor: These verses occur in the previous anecdote and have already been explained.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r1.claim: Shuʿayb belonged to Midian, explaining the earlier wording their brother Shuʿayb; here he addresses the people of the thicket without being one of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r1.anchor: وكان شعيب عليه السلام من أهل مدين، فلذلك جاء: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r2.claim: A report identifies the people of the thicket with the people of Midian.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r2.anchor: ومن غريب النقل ما روي عن ابن عباس، أن أصحاب الأيكة هم أصحاب مدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r3.claim: Another report distinguishes the thicket's rural people from the inhabitants of Midian's town.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p186/r3.anchor: وعن غيره، أن أصحاب الأيكة هم أهل البادية، وأصحاب مدين هم الحاضرة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r1.claim: The opening says that Shuayb spoke to them but does not call him their brother.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r1.anchor: ولم يقل أخوهم وقيل ( الأيكة ) الشجر الملتف

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r2.claim: Some identify the wood as a thicket of interwoven trees, including the dawma tree; alternatively, al-ayka is the entire country like Mecca and Bakka, and on either view its people are distinct from Madyan, despite an unusual report from Ibn Abbas equating them.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r2.anchor: وقيل ( الأيكة ) الشجر الملتف وكان شجرهم الدوم وهو المقل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r3.speaker: الحرميان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r3.claim: The two readers of the Haramain and Ibn Amir read layka with a fatḥa on lām and no alif, treating it as a diptote here and in Sad.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان وابن عامر ( ليكة ) بلام مفتوحة بعدها ياء بغير الف

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda says an exegesis book calls Layka the name of a settlement.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : وجدنا في بعض كتب التفسير ان ( ليكة ) اسم للقرية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says readers using the accusative mistakenly take Layka, written without alif in the codex, as a place name; the codex may spell these two occurrences phonetically, as in the treatment of other forms, while the story is one and Layka is unknown.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r5.anchor: وفي الكشاف من قرأ بالنصب وزعم أن ( ليكة ) بوزن ليلة اسماسم بلد

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r6.claim: The author's response calls the claim unsupported: the reading is among the seven and is mutawatir, with a further report from a tafsir book.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r6.anchor: وتعقب بانه دعوى من غير ثبت وكفى ثبتا للمخالف ثبوت القراءة في السبعة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r7.speaker: البخاري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r7.claim: Al-Bukhari's Sahih has both forms, al-Ayka and Layka, glossed as the thicket.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r7.anchor: روى البخاري في صحيحه 0 الأيكة ) وليكة الغيضة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r8.claim: Even if the Arabic root l-y-k is unattested, the word may be foreign; non-Arabic roots often differ, and the name can be diptote for being proper, foreign, and feminine.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r8.anchor: إن صح لايضر وتكون الكلمة عجمية ومواد كلام العجم مخالفة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r9.claim: The author says denying this mutawatir reading approaches apostasy, noting that al-Mubarrad, Ibn Qutayba, al-Zajjaj, al-Farisi, and al-Nahhas preceded al-Zamakhshari in rejecting it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r9.anchor: انكار الزمخشري صحة هذه القراءة يقرب من الردة والعياذ بالله

ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r10.claim: Layka is also read with the hamza deleted and its vowel shifted onto lām, and is written according to its pronunciation, unlike the spelling with hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p117#4/r10.anchor: وقريء ( ليكة ) بحذف الهمزة والقاء حركتها على اللام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p127/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p127/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p127/r7.claim: Shuayb is not called their brother among the people of the thicket because he was not related to them, but is called Madyan's brother because he belonged to them; God sent him to both groups.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p127/r7.anchor: ولم يقل أخوهم؛ لأنه لم يكن من أصحاب الأيكة في النسب، فلما ذكر مدين قال أخاهم شعيبا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p127/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p127/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p127/r8.claim: The prophets' calls share a form because they agree on piety, obedience, sincere worship, and refusing payment for preaching and conveying the message.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p127/r8.anchor: وإنما كانت دعوة هؤلاء الأنبياء كلهم فيما حكى الله عنهم على صيغة واحدة

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:172-177/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:172-177/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:172-177/r2.claim: Al-Aykah is a grove of soft trees near Midian whose people received Shuʿayb as an outsider, explaining why he is not called their brother; another view identifies it as an intertwined dawmah tree.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:172-177/r2.anchor: الأيكة غيضة تنبت ناعم الشجر يريد غيضة بقرب مدين تسكنها طائفة فبعث الله إليهن شعيبا كما بعثه إلى مدين

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:172-177/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:172-177/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:172-177/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Ibn Amir read Laykah without hamza, moving its vowel to the lām; another form has fatḥa as a town name, and spelling omits alif to follow pronunciation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:172-177/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر «ليكة» بحذف الهمزة وإبقاء حركتها على اللام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r7.claim: Shuʿayb is not called their brother because he was a city dweller addressing pastoral people; the passage says prophets were sent from towns, honoring settled communities for their shared wisdom and blessing.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r7.anchor: ولم يقل : أخوهم , إشارة إلى أنه لم يرسل نبيا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r8.claim: Taqwa means fear of God, which is what Shuʿayb commands when asking whether they will not be reverent.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r8.anchor: تكونون من أهل التقو , وهو مخافة من الله سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r12.claim: All messengers agree in calling people to fear, obey, and worship God sincerely, while showing counsel, integrity, honesty, and restraint from seeking payment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p385/r12.anchor: اتضح أن الرسل متطابقون في الدعوة في الأمر بالتقوى

THALABI:v7p177/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p177/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p177/r7.claim: The destruction is a sign; most of Lot's people did not believe, and God is mighty and merciful.
THALABI:v7p177/r7.anchor: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r5.claim: The al-Aykah passage omits “their brother” because Shuʿayb was not one of that people; he was the brother of Midian and was sent to both groups.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r5.anchor: وذلك أن شعيباً ليس من أصحاب الأيكة وإنما هو أخو مدين

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r6.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r6.claim: Al-Kashshāf gives the same explanation for omitting “their brother” in the al-Aykah account: Shuʿayb was not from them.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r6.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) : "فإن قلت: هلا قيل: (أخوهم شعيب) كما في سائر المواضع؟ قلت: إِنَّ شعيباً

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r7.speaker: الحديث
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r7.claim: A hadith cited by al-Kashshāf says Shuʿayb, the brother of Midian, was sent to Midian and to the people of al-Aykah.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث: "إن شعيباً أخا مدين أُرسل إيهم وإلى أصحاب الأيكة"

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r10.claim: Differences of mention and omission have varied contextual causes, all reflecting attention to the setting and selection of the most apt expression.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#9/r10.anchor: وكلها ترجع إلى مراعاة المقام وحسن الاختيار وذكر اللفظة في الوضع الذي يقتضيها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.claim: Samarrāʾī distinguishes Midian from the Aykah people: Shuaib belonged to Midian, so he is called their brother when addressing Midian but not Aykah; the other Shuʿara prophets address their own peoples.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#6/r1.anchor: ومدين غير أصحاب الأيكة، وشعيب عليه السلام كان من مدين ولم يكن من أصحاب الأيكة ولذلك إذا ذكرت مدين قال: (أخوهم)
